모델: E50 눈 — LAB 편 전체를 영상으로(제작 절차 lab-whole-video). 11-24에 구운 펠트 판 일곱 장을 시작 · 끝 그림으로 쓴다. 공통 글은 M76 지시문의 공통 글에 떠 있는 몽글 · 눈송이 · 친구 줄을 더했다
공통: One continuous shot, no cuts. The camera is locked off exactly as in the start frame: no zoom, no pan, no tilt, no shake. Keep the exact handmade needle-felt miniature look of the start frame in every frame: fine wool felt fibres, visible stitches, matte felt and wool; every object keeps its shape, size and colour and never turns into a realistic thing. MONGLE is the coral-pink felt blob. At rest its face is only its two glossy black bead eyes: no nose and no mouth. When its feeling changes, its whole face changes to show that feeling, as written in ACTION, always in needle-felt: the eyes may grow bigger and rounder, squeeze shut into short curved dark stitched lines, curve into happy arcs or droop under little felt lids; a small simple felt mouth may open, smile, pout or wobble; blush, a felt sweat drop or a felt teardrop may appear. When the feeling passes, the mouth and the drops go away and the face returns to rest. Open eyes always stay glossy black beads: no white sclera, no eyelashes, no human teeth or lips. Mongle has NO arms, NO legs, NO hands and NO neck, ever: no limbs ever grow, nothing ever sticks out of its body. It moves only by tilting, squashing, stretching and bouncing its whole soft dome body. LOOK: the same light and colours as the start frame, unchanged to the last frame. Apart from Mongle's own expression, nothing new appears that is not in the start frame. No speed lines, no motion lines, no cartoon effects, no steam, no smoke. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos. No sound.

클립.prompt: The first-snow evening street from the start frame: the friend stands on the left already touching the skin just under his own eye with one fingertip, Mongle floats on the right looking up, its face at rest. ACTION: from 0 to 0.3 s Mongle tips its dome up toward the snowy sky; from 0.3 to 1.1 s its face lights up with joy - its eyes curve into two happy dark stitched arcs and a small open smiling felt mouth appears - and it gives one happy little bob; from 1.2 s its face goes back to rest, round black bead eyes and no mouth, looking at the friend. At about 1.2 s the friend taps the spot under his eye twice with his fingertip, raises his eyebrows and tilts his head like asking a question, smiling with closed lips. The few snowflakes drift slowly down. The friend is the young felt man with the mustard knit beanie, cream scarf and charcoal padded coat: his face, hair and clothes stay exactly the same in every frame. Mongle floats just above the ground, as in the start frame. The few white felt snowflakes keep their size and only drift; no extra snow, no snow particles, no dots fill the air. Mongle never grows arms or legs. The air around Mongle stays clean: only the real felt objects of the start and end frames are ever visible, nothing is drawn over the picture.

Medium close shot of the friend from the start frame, pointing at his own eye with his index finger. ACTION: both round black bead eyes stay wide open the whole time, shining, looking straight ahead; the eyes never close and never blink. From 0 to 1.6 s his fingertip moves a little closer to his eye on the right side of the picture and taps the cheek just under that eye two times, clearly showing the open eye. From 1.8 s to the end he nods a little with a proud closed-lip smile, the fingertip resting on the cheek just under the open eye. The skin between the fingertip and the eye is clean felt: no line, no thread, no lash. Only the friend is in this shot; the two snowflakes drift slowly. The friend is the young felt man with the mustard knit beanie, cream scarf and charcoal padded coat: his face, hair and clothes stay exactly the same in every frame. No extra snow, no snow particles, no dots fill the air. Nothing is drawn over the picture.

Low close shot of Mongle from the start frame, looking up at the biggest white felt snowflake high above it in the evening sky. ACTION: from 0 to 2.6 s Mongle sways gently, gazing up, delighted: a small open smiling felt mouth appears at about 0.4 s and stays while the biggest snowflake turns slowly in the air and sinks a little. At 2.8 s the smile goes away and Mongle watches the flake, eyes round. From 3.0 s the biggest snowflake drops faster, straight down toward Mongle's face; at about 3.8 s it lands flat right on Mongle's eye on the left and sticks there, covering that eye completely, with two or three tiny crumbs of felt snow, exactly as in the end frame. As it lands Mongle's soft dome sinks a little and comes back up, and its face changes to a surprised face: its other bead eye becomes bigger and perfectly round and a small round felt mouth of dark burgundy felt opens, exactly as in the end frame. From 4.4 s to the end the snowflake stays stuck and Mongle's open eye blinks twice. Mongle floats just above the ground, as in the start frame. The few white felt snowflakes keep their size and only drift; no extra snow, no snow particles, no dots fill the air. Mongle never grows arms or legs. The air around Mongle stays clean: only the real felt objects of the start and end frames are ever visible, nothing is drawn over the picture.

The friend is the young felt man with the mustard knit beanie, cream scarf and charcoal padded coat: his face, hair and clothes stay exactly the same in every frame. From 1.5 s to the end Mongle bobs gently and its open bead eye blinks twice. The stuck snowflake stays exactly in place on Mongle's eye. Low close shot of Mongle from the start frame: one white felt snowflake already stuck over its eye on the left, its other bead eye open and its small round mouth open. The snowflake over the left eye stays stuck there, unchanged, from the very first frame to the very last frame. The open eye on the right is one solid glossy black bead with no white part: it stays a plain round black bead and does not roll or look around. ACTION: from 0.2 to 0.8 s a second white felt snowflake of the same size sinks down from above, right over the open eye, turning slowly. At 0.9 s it lands flat right on the open eye, covering it completely, exactly as in the end frame, and a soft white cap of felt snow is left on top of its head. As it lands its mouth opens into a wide wavy felt mouth, with rosy cheeks and one small pale-blue felt sweat drop on the side of its head, exactly as in the end frame. From 1.2 s to the end Mongle has both eyes covered: it tips its dome left, then right, then left again, wobbling like a spinning top slowing down, its mouth wobbling open the whole time. Both snowflakes stay stuck. Mongle floats just above the ground, as in the start frame.
